note: The About page’s words. The cards are set in a serif font that has no straight apostrophe and no slash: use the curly apostrophe (’) and write around slashes. “watching” and “reading” are the two small cards about the last movie or series you watched and the book you are reading: change “text” when it changes. Their “Suggest me” link opens an email to you with “subject” already filled in; the subject is not shown on the page, so a slash is fine there.
portraitNote: I didn’t have many photos of myself to begin with.

who.title: Who
paragraphs: I’m Romit Raj Sahu, a CS student in Bangalore, India. I absolutely love computers, and I keep discovering something new every single day. Most of what I know started with a curious search. I stay humble and keep learning more about things I think I already know (because trust me, I know a little about a lot of things).
I currently work in full stack and DevOps. I try to keep my knowledge as deep and as broad as I can, so that I’m the one you reach out to when something breaks.

tinkering.title: Whereabouts
paragraphs: Right now I’m relearning things I learnt a long time ago, to better understand the code being written. I also keep tinkering with my server and deploying things on it.

contact.title: Contact
paragraphs: I’m open to internships and full-time roles. If you have something interesting, say hi.
Email is the fastest way to reach me: {email}. There is also a resume, if you want it.

key.note: The OpenPGP key under the Contact card. Its facts (fingerprint, key ID, algorithms, expiry) are read from the key itself, src/assets/files/romitraj-pgp-public.asc; these are only the words around them. 'uses' names what each part of the key is for; 'and' joins the algorithms. In 'fetch' and 'command', {email} is the address from site.json. 'copy' and 'copied' are the copy button's words before and after a press; 'copyLabel' is what screen readers hear for it.
